paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the Pass@1 Rate (%) as a function of the Number of Reasoning Steps. The x-axis is labeled "Num. of Reasoning Steps" and uses an exponential scale, ranging from 0 to 40 with tick labels at 5,10,20, and 40. The y-axis is labeled "Pass@1 Rate (%)" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 100 with tick labels at intervals of 20. There are two lines in the plot. The first line, representing "GPT-4o", is depicted in blue with circular markers and a solid line style. It starts at 6.5% at 5 reasoning steps, increases to 32.3% at 10 steps, then moves to 77.4% at 20 steps, and ultimately reaches 83.9% at 40 steps. The second line, representing "Claude-3.5-Sonnet", is shown in a similar blue color with star markers and a dashed line style. It begins at 19.4% at 5 reasoning steps, rises to 38.7% at 10 steps, further increases to 87.1% at 20 steps, and reaches a final value of 89.2% at 40 steps. Both lines show an increasing trend in "Pass@1 Rate(%)" as "Num. of Reasoning Steps" increases. There is a legend box on the top of the plot to identify the lines of "GPT-4o" and "Claude-3.5-Sonnet".
